thread:
Maria K: Heads up — spike in schema.reject_count for toolhooks on the canary after we flipped strict validate. Most rejects are 'missing field' but a few raw samples include unredacted user content. cc @Jon @Samir :warning:

Jon: Do we have sampling on for rejected payloads? I thought console samples were always redacted by default.

Samir: We have sampling but recently a debug change reduced redaction in the sample exporter. That change was supposed to be gated behind an internal flag.

Irene L: Running a quick query: `metric(schema.rejects).by(tool).window(5m)` — looks pretty noisy. Can someone paste an example sample?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout 'strict-validate-toolhook' -> 22% traffic, stage 1 complete.

Maria K: Putting an example I grabbed (manually redacted): ```{ "user": "[REDACTED]", "input": "Order #12345: cc1234..." }``` — noticed some entries in the console export weren't redacted.

Jon: That's bad. Two quick ones: (1) are we persisting raw rejected payloads anywhere long-term? (2) can we switch to storing only hashes + schema-diff for the console view?

Samir: We persist raw rejects to the 'reject-bucket' for 7 days for debugging. Sampling default is 1%. A recent canary config accidentally set sampling to 100% for the canary slice while debugging. That explains the volume.

Irene L: UX note: Console currently shows an 'Example rejection' card with a toggle 'Show raw sample'. That toggle bypasses redaction if the viewer has the debug role. Canary envs had that permission enabled for the platform team.

Jon: Proposal: always redact by default in the main console. Provide an 'Escalate for debugging' flow that requires an auditable SRE approval before unredacted samples are shown. No direct bypass toggle.

Samir: Telemetry suggestion: emit `schema.unredacted_sample_exposure_count` when a raw sample is viewed and tag events with `canary=true/false` + `sampling_rate`. Also add `fallback.model` to the reject log so we know which compat model handled a request.

Maria K: Also observed: routing fallback for rejects currently sends requests to a compat model that strips fields differently than prod. Canary used a custom fallback dev-model which likely dropped fields — causing the 'missing field' rejects. We should log fallback identity.

Jon: Agreed. Action items: Samir — revert canary sampling to 1% and add the new metric; Irene — change console default to redact and implement escalate workflow; Maria — open an incident/ticket and coordinate legal review if any PII surfaced.

console-bot: console-bot: Created task PLAT-4217: "console: default redact for rejected samples" and linked to #eng-platform.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling back canary flag `unredacted_debug_samples` to false in ~10m.

Maria K: :thumbsup: Thanks all. I'll collect counts for the postmortem and add a short runbook entry for canary sampling flags.
